title: Sudden CEO death and firm value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Event Study with a market-model benchmark.  
Why: A sudden CEO death is an unexpected, exogenous shock that is idiosyncratic to the firm. By comparing realised returns during the event window [0,+1] to the counterfactual returns predicted by the market model (estimated in the pre-event window [−10,−2]), we isolate the abnormal part of the return that can be causally attributed to the shock.  

Key assumptions  
1. No information leakage: the market learns about the death only at t = 0.  
2. Market efficiency: prices incorporate the shock immediately; hence any effect appears in [0,+1].  
3. Correct model of normal returns: the linear market model fitted in [−10,−2] accurately captures expected returns in the absence of the shock.  
4. No confounding events affecting many firms simultaneously (cross-sectional independence for the t-test).  

## 2. R Code
```r
# ---------------------------------------------
# Sudden CEO death event study
# ---------------------------------------------
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# 1. Read the data -----------------------------------------------------------
dat_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s12_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(dat_path)

# 2. Define windows ----------------------------------------------------------
est_window  <- -10:-2          # estimation window
event_window <- 0:1            # main event window

# 3. Estimate firm-level market models --------------------------------------
# Run:  ret_it = alpha_i + beta_i * mkt_ret_t  (t in [-10,-2])
betas <- df %>%
  filter(event_day %in% est_window) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do(tidy(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(stock_id, term, estimate) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = term,
                     values_from = estimate,
                     names_prefix = "") %>%
  rename(alpha = `(Intercept)`, beta_est = mkt_ret)

# 4. Compute abnormal returns (AR) ------------------------------------------
df_ar <- df %>%
  inner_join(betas, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - (alpha + beta_est * mkt_ret))

# 5. Cumulate abnormal returns over [0,+1] -----------------------------------
car_firm <- df_ar %>%
  filter(event_day %in% event_window) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop")

# 6. Portfolio-level statistics ---------------------------------------------
N  <- nrow(car_firm)
avg_CAR <- mean(car_firm$CAR)
sd_CAR  <- sd(car_firm$CAR)
t_stat  <- avg_CAR / (sd_CAR / sqrt(N))
p_value <- 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = N - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)  # two-sided

cat("Main result: Average CAR[0,+1]\n")
cat("Number of firms :", N, "\n")
cat("Mean CAR        :", round(avg_CAR, 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic     :", round(t_stat, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value         :", round(p_value, 4), "\n\n")

# 7. Robustness checks -------------------------------------------------------
# (a) Market-adjusted returns: AR = ret - mkt_ret
car_simple <- df %>%
  filter(event_day %in% event_window) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_simple = sum(ret - mkt_ret), .groups = "drop")

avg_CAR_s  <- mean(car_simple$CAR_simple)
sd_CAR_s   <- sd(car_simple$CAR_simple)
t_s        <- avg_CAR_s / (sd_CAR_s / sqrt(N))

cat("Robustness: Market-adjusted model\n")
cat("Mean CAR_simple :", round(avg_CAR_s, 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic     :", round(t_s, 3), "\n\n")

# (b) Alternative event window [0,+2]
car_alt <- df_ar %>%
  filter(event_day %in% 0:2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_0_2 = sum(AR), .groups = "drop")

avg_CAR_alt <- mean(car_alt$CAR_0_2)
cat("Robustness: CAR[0,+2] average =", round(avg_CAR_alt, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Because CEO deaths are typically interpreted as negative news (loss of leadership, potential strategic disruption), I expect the average CAR over [0,+1] to be negative—around −1% to −2% (−0.010 to −0.020). Given 80 events, the t-statistic should be around −3 to −5, indicating statistical significance at the 1% level.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — market model AR; estimation [−10,−2]; event window [0,+1]
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms experience significant negative CAR on CEO death announcement
